observation_summary: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method fails to correctly preserve or update the year when parsing partial date strings (like month-only or month-day). The resulting date often defaults to the year 2000 or another incorrect year instead of maintaining the base year provided in the MutableDateTime object.
hypothesis: The parsing logic in DateTimeFormatter.parseInto incorrectly resets or fails to correctly propagate the year field when only partial date information is provided. It likely uses an incorrect default year or fails to correctly merge the parsed partial date with the existing state of the MutableDateTime object.
prediction: The code responsible for parsing partial dates will show an incorrect assignment or calculation of the year field, likely defaulting to a hardcoded value (like 2000) or failing to correctly extract the year from the base object before applying the parsed month/day.
experiment_rationale: The failure consistently shows the year being reset to 2000 (or another incorrect year) regardless of the input, indicating a flaw in the procedural logic that handles the merging of parsed partial date components into the target object.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a procedural error in how the date parsing algorithm merges partial date information into an existing date object. It is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple wrong constant (Assignment), but a flaw in the logic that determines the year during the parsing process. Therefore, it is classified as Algorithm/Method.
evidence_gaps: The actual production code implementation of parseInto is not provided, only the test cases demonstrating the failure.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not just a wrong constant value, but a failure in the logic that determines the year during the parsing process.
There is no evidence of a missing guard or validation check; the logic itself is performing the wrong operation.
